purpose: Expressive four-panel gag comic before the gameplay guide.
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: funny four-panel comic atlas used inside an actual fantasy dungeon repair puzzle game.
Generate a NEW comedy-comic version of the story. Reference 1 is only the established dungeon, mechanic and skeleton character identity, NOT the old solemn staging. Reference 2 is the mechanic's exact costume: teal hood, brass goggles, brown apron and work gloves.
One landscape 4:3 image, preferably 2048x1536, exactly four equally sized panels in a 2x2 grid with divisions at x=50%, y=50%. No margins or gutters. Every quadrant is a self-contained 4:3 scene cropped at runtime.
VISUAL STYLE: lively hand-inked Korean fantasy gag webtoon, bold expressive outlines, bright flat cel-shaded colors, exaggerated funny faces and gestures, squash-and-stretch chibi acting, comic action lines, sweat drops, surprise marks and little dust puffs. Clear visual comedy, warm readable teal-and-brass dungeon palette, friendly goofy skeletons. Definitely cartoon storytelling instead of a solemn 3D cinematic still. No gore.
LAYOUT: in every panel, the upper 25% is quiet dim dungeon wall with NO faces or essential props: the game overlays two speech balloons there. Put the left speaker around x=25%-35%, y=50%-65% and the right speaker around x=65%-80%, y=50%-65% of EACH panel. Essential actions in middle and lower-middle. Keep bottom 10% quiet floor. DO NOT draw speech bubbles, text, letters, sound-effect words or watermarks; all dialogue and effects are added by code.
TOP LEFT / 1: A ridiculously self-satisfied armored hero with a flowing red cape, on the LEFT, struts up a short stair toward a bright doorway while proudly holding a detached CARTOON skeleton arm like a trophy. A disassembled skeleton guard on the RIGHT frantically reaches after him with its remaining hand, jaw wide open in comic protest. Broken brass spike traps, scattered gears and bones show the hero's mess. The hero is oblivious and thinks the mission is complete. Hero and guard faces both clearly visible in profile or 3/4.
TOP RIGHT / 2: Our teal-hooded dungeon mechanic on the LEFT has a deadpan exhausted expression, half-lidded eyes, slumped shoulders, one giant sweat drop, carrying a wrench. On the RIGHT, a very cheerful skeleton skull sits on a wooden crate, its disconnected cartoon body bones neatly collapsed beside it. The skull is happily reporting for work despite not having a body. Comical contrast in expressions, surrounding ruined dungeon.
BOTTOM LEFT / 3: Same mechanic on the LEFT tries to reassemble the skeleton on the RIGHT at a workbench. The mechanic holds an OBVIOUS BARE SKELETAL FOOT up beside the skeleton's shoulder socket, about to mistake it for a hand. The skeleton looks down at the foot, comically horrified, pointing with its remaining real hand. The foot's heel and toes must be obvious, no boot. Mechanic freezes with embarrassed sweat. Nearby a partly repaired brass trap and gear identify the repair job. One funny reaction burst, not violence.
BOTTOM RIGHT / 4: Same mechanic on LEFT stands safely next to the exit and has proudly pulled a brass lever. The restored skeleton guard on RIGHT stands on the far side of the raised floor spikes, pointing at the mechanic's forgotten brown TOOLBOX on the far side next to its own feet. Mechanic suddenly realizes the mistake, enormous shocked eyes, open mouth and sweat drops; the skeleton gives a cheeky friendly grin. Trap spikes stand between the mechanic and the forgotten toolbox, all characters safe. The joke is that the repair is complete but the toolbox is stranded. Safe exit doorway remains behind mechanic on LEFT. No one is injured. Make the toolbox clearly visible.
Preserve the same mechanic and recurring skeleton identity through all panels. All comedic objects and gestures readable. No text anywhere.
